h: Herons, hides and a North East day out
p: WWT Washington is a lovely size for a family outing: big enough to feel like a proper adventure, small enough that nobody's dragging their feet by the end. Spring is a brilliant time to come, when the grey herons are busy nesting in the woodland, and you can keep an eye on the comings and goings of the heronry. Later in the year the wildflower meadows burst into colour and the butterflies and dragonflies come out to play, so summer feels very different from the moody winter months when ducks crowd on to the ponds.

Woodland birds are another highlight. Bullfinches, tits and woodpeckers often show well around the feeders, which is a great chance for kids to get a close look without needing binoculars. The hides overlooking the River Wear side of the reserve are the spot to pause, listen and count what you can see.

Give yourself a couple of hours to wander round at a relaxed pace, or longer with little ones who'll want to stop at every pond. Bring a waterproof, as North East weather has a mind of its own, and wellies are handy after a wet spell.

There's plenty to stack around it. Penshaw Monument, the Greek-temple-style landmark on the hill, is close by and a short climb rewards you with big views over Wearside. Herrington Country Park sits at its foot for a walk or a picnic, and Durham's cathedral and castle are within easy reach for a bit of history to round things off. Sunderland's seafront is there too when the kids start asking about the beach.
